senses.gloss:
Aṃśu.--I. Name of a protégé of the Aśvins in the Rigveda. 2. dhānaṃjayya, pupil of Amāvāsya śāṇḍilyāyana, according to the vaṃśa brāhmaṇa.
Foot notes viii. 5, 26. Cf. Ludwig, Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 160; Hopkins, Journal of the American Oriental Society, 17, 89; Sieg, Die Sagenstoffe des ṛgveda, 129, suggests that he may be identical with khela.
Indische Studien, 4, 373.
